newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers predict sharp fall in grain yields.
newsitem.headline: French farmers predict sharp fall in grain yields.

text.p: France's largest farm union added to fears of mounting drought damage on Friday by predicting that a three-month dry spell had done irreversible harm to winter grain crops.

"All winter grain crops -- soft wheat, durum wheat, barley, malting barley -- are suffering from the lack of rain. Even if water tables recovered in coming weeks, we would see a sharp fall in yields," the FNSEA said in a statement.
FNSEA issued the prediction after its special drought crisis team met earlier in the day to review the crop situation.

FNSEA also predicted "bad" yields for sunflower, adding that in many cases farmers would have to sow their fields again. Dry soils were also hampering maize sowings and the next 10 to 15 days would be crucial.
Persisting dry conditions have forced farmers to feed cattle with fodder they would have normally kept for summer and winter stocks.
"The level of fodder stocks is currently their main concern," the statement said. The drought crisis team will hold its next meeting on May 29.
